detail:
The Reflex Sympathetic Dystrophy Syndrome Association (RSDSA) newsletter reports on CRPS-RISE, a placebo-controlled clinical trial studying investigational neridronate in early, warm-subtype CRPS type 1. According to the newsletter, the trial enrolls people in an early stage of type 1 disease whose affected limb shows the warm presentation, and compares the investigational treatment against placebo on pain and other outcomes. Neridronate is described as investigational for this use: it is being studied in the trial and is not presented as an established or approved CRPS treatment.

The RSDSA coverage presents the trial as part of a broader effort to test treatments in a defined early subtype of CRPS, on the reasoning in sources that earlier, more uniform disease may respond differently than long-standing CRPS. The newsletter does not report the therapy as proven: sources note that placebo-controlled results are what determine whether the approach works, and that findings in early warm-subtype type 1 disease would not automatically extend to other CRPS types or stages.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about complex regional pain syndrome research and clinical trials.
summary: An RSDSA newsletter covers CRPS-RISE, a placebo-controlled trial of investigational neridronate in early warm-subtype CRPS type 1, framed as an unproven approach being tested in a defined early subtype.
takeaways: CRPS-RISE is a placebo-controlled trial in early warm-subtype type 1 disease
neridronate is investigational for CRPS, not an established treatment
results in one early subtype would not automatically extend to all CRPS
title: Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS): an investigational trial in early warm-subtype disease
